experiment: Skipped — all four goals (freshness, diversity, multi-source, educational value) are within targets, no experiment is active, and no pause gate is set. The one queued experiment (numerical-density) targets scripts/write-prompt.md, which is out of scope for daily parameter tuning.
weakestArea: No metric is below target. The thinnest margin is regional spread: five regions ship (≥4 floor met) but Oceania is absent and sub-Saharan Africa sits at just 3 of 50; the top four regions (EU/AM/AS/ME) are evenly balanced at 10-13 each with no concentration problem. Sci-tech share also eased from 42% to 34% as science fell 11→7, still comfortably above the 25% floor.
watching: Science dropped to 7 (from 11 yesterday) — above its ≥5 floor but the softest educational input; watch that it doesn't slide under the floor on a light-news day.
Throughput rebounded to 50 with all five cycles completing, versus 38 yesterday when one cycle failed — reliability looks recovered, confirm it holds.
Multi-source count is unusually high at 16 (vs 9 yesterday), reflecting a heavy politics/economy day (33 of 50) with strong event clustering.
coverageGaps: Oceania (OC) had zero articles today, the second consecutive thin day for the region.
Sub-Saharan Africa (AF) remains the lowest region at 3 despite curated regional sources — a persistent structural thinness, not a one-day dip.
context: All six goal metrics are met with healthy margins and zero duplicates; top source share is only 8% with five outlets tied at 4, so source concentration is a non-issue. This was a high-volume, politics-heavy day (politics 19, economy 14) with 55 unique sources and 16 multi-source articles. No experiment is active, no gate is set, and no tunable parameter is out of range, so this is a hold day with no change. The only recurring editorial note — thin Africa/Oceania coverage — is a feed-composition/source-list matter to revisit deliberately, not something to move on a single day's data.
